item.title: Deploying Jekyll Chirpy on GitHub Pages: The Complete Setup, CI/CD Pipeline, and Bug-Fix Playbook
item.description:
Setting up a documentation portal or department blog using the Jekyll Chirpy theme on GitHub Pages looks effortless on paper. You fork the starter repo, point GitHub Actions to your branch, and watch the site spin up.

In reality, running a production-grade Chirpy setup with custom CI/CD pipelines quickly runs into a minefield of build-time failures: Ruby Liquid crashes over integer tags, htmlproofer throwing hundreds of false-positive 404s on dynamic taxonomy routes, missing local layout overrides, broken anchor fragment checks, and invisible non-breaking spaces that crash YAML parsers.

item.title: GitHub Actions: Complete CI/CD Guide from Beginner to Production
item.description:
GitHub Actions: Complete CI/CD Guide from Beginner to Production

Writing code is only one part of software development.

Modern software teams automate everything:

  • Building applications
  • Running tests
  • Checking code quality
  • Creating Docker images
  • Publishing releases
  • Deploying applications
  • Sending notifications

GitHub Actions makes all of this possible without leaving GitHub.

Whether you’re building a personal portfolio or managing enterprise software, GitHub Actions helps you deliver software faster, more reliably, and with fewer mistakes.

item.title: Docker: Complete Beginner to Production Guide
item.description:
Docker: Complete Beginner to Production Guide

Docker changed software development by making applications portable and predictable. Instead of saying, “It works on my machine,” developers can package an application with everything it needs—code, libraries, runtime, and dependencies—into a container that runs consistently anywhere.

Docker has become a standard tool for developers, DevOps engineers, cloud engineers, and platform teams.

In this guide, you’ll learn Docker from the ground up and build production-ready containerized applications.

item.title: Python for DevOps and Automation: Complete Beginner to Advanced Guide
item.description:
Python for DevOps and Automation: Complete Beginner to Advanced Guide

Python has become the language of choice for automation, cloud engineering, DevOps, data processing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and backend development.

Its clean syntax, extensive standard library, and rich ecosystem make it one of the most productive programming languages available.

Whether you want to automate repetitive tasks, build APIs, manage cloud infrastructure, analyze logs, or deploy applications, Python is an essential skill.

item.title: Git & GitHub: Complete Beginner to Advanced Guide for Modern Development
item.description:
Git & GitHub: Complete Beginner to Advanced Guide for Modern Development

Git is the most widely used version control system in the world. Whether you’re building a personal website, contributing to open source, or deploying applications to the cloud, Git is an essential skill.

Git keeps track of every change you make, while GitHub provides a platform to store repositories, collaborate with others, automate workflows, and publish projects.

In this guide, you’ll learn Git from scratch and build habits used by professional software teams.

item.title: The 90-Day Blueprint to Becoming a Full-Stack Developer: From Zero to AI-Powered Apps
item.description:
Ninety days sounds tight. If you ask ten senior engineers how long it takes to become job-ready, most will say a year or two. They aren’t lying, but they are assuming traditional computer science degree timelines or casual self-study. If you cut out the noise, focus on production-grade tools, and ship real projects every single week, three months is plenty of time to build a formidable foundation.

This blueprint breaks down the exact 90-day trajectory. We start with raw web fundamentals, move into modern frontend architectures, build scalable backends, automate infrastructure with DevOps, and wrap up by wiring AI intelligence directly into full-stack applications.
